titleEn: Silky Red Lentil Soup with Mint Butter
description: The quintessential national starter of Turkey: pureed crimson lentils gently simmered with aromatic vegetables, strained to a velvety sheen, and crowned with bubbling dried mint and paprika infused butter.

ingredients.name: Turkish Sweet Pepper Paste (Tatlı Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: 1 tbsp tomato paste mixed with 1/2 tsp smoked paprika

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Standard dried spearmint or dried peppermint

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: 3/4 tsp sweet Hungarian paprika mixed with 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper

steps.instruction: Roughly chop the onion, carrot, and potato. In a large heavy-bottomed Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté the vegetables until onion is translucent and soft.
Stir in the Turkish sweet pepper paste and ground cumin, blooming the paste in the fragrant oil until fragrant and slightly deepened in color.
Thoroughly rinse red lentils under cold water until water runs clear. Add the rinsed lentils and broth to the pot. Bring to a rapid rolling boil, skimming any foam from the surface.
Reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer until lentils and vegetables are thoroughly tender and falling apart.

Puree the soup until completely smooth using an immersion blender, then pour through a fine-mesh sieve (süzgeç) for an authentically silky restaurant texture. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

In a small skillet or cezve, melt butter over medium-low heat until foaming. Stir in dried spearmint and Aleppo pepper; sizzle for 30 seconds until aromatic, then drizzle over ladled bowls and serve with fresh lemon wedges.

titleEn: Ezogelin Soup with Bulgur, Rice, and Mint
description: Named after the legendary Anatolian bride Ezo, this textured and zesty soup unites red lentils with bulgur wheat and rice in a fragrant tomato-pepper broth laced with dried mint.

ingredients.name: Coarse Bulgur Wheat (Pilavlık Bulgur)
ingredients.substitute: Coarse bulgur #3 (available at Whole Foods) or cracked wheat

ingredients.name: Baldo Rice or White Rice
ingredients.substitute: Arborio rice or Calrose medium-grain white rice

ingredients.name: Turkish Hot Pepper Paste (Acı Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: 1 tbsp tomato paste mixed with 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Dried spearmint

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Red pepper chili flakes mixed with a pinch of paprika

steps.instruction: Rinse red lentils, bulgur, and rice together in a fine mesh colander. Place them in a soup pot with the broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer partially covered until grains are tender.
While grains cook, finely dice the onion and mince garlic. In a separate saucepan, melt butter with olive oil over medium heat and sauté onion until caramelized at edges.
Add minced garlic, tomato paste, and hot pepper paste to the onions. Cook, stirring constantly, until the pastes release their rich aromatic oils.
Whisk in dried spearmint and Aleppo pepper into the paste mixture, sizzling gently for 30 seconds to infuse.

Ladle one cup of hot lentil broth into the tomato-paste pan to temper and loosen it, then pour everything back into the main soup pot. Whisk vigorously so the grains partially crush without turning into a smooth puree.
Simmer together over low heat for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Season with salt, and serve piping hot with lemon wedges.

description: Originating from Anatolian mountain pastures, this soothing comfort soup features tender rice enveloped in a velvety tempered yogurt broth, garnished with sizzling mint-infused butter.

ingredients.name: Turkish Strained Yogurt (Süzme Yoğurt)
ingredients.substitute: Plain whole-milk Greek yogurt (e.g. Fage Total 5%)

ingredients.name: Baldo Rice or Short-Grain Rice
ingredients.substitute: Arborio or Calrose short-grain white rice

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.substitute: Cornstarch (for gluten-free variation)

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Standard dried spearmint

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Pinch of paprika and red pepper flakes

steps.instruction: In a medium saucepan, combine the rice and 5 cups of water or broth. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then lower heat and simmer until rice grains are very soft.
In a mixing bowl, prepare the terbiye (liason): whisk together yogurt, egg yolk, all-purpose flour, and 1/4 cup room-temperature water until completely smooth without any lumps.
CRITICAL TEMPERING STEP: Slowly ladle two ladles of hot rice water into the yogurt bowl one splash at a time while whisking vigorously, raising the yogurt's temperature to prevent curdling.
Turn heat under the pot to low. Pour the tempered yogurt mixture into the pot in a steady stream, stirring continuously in one direction until the soup returns to a gentle simmer.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes, continuing to stir periodically. Turn off heat and ONLY NOW stir in salt (adding salt early curdles yogurt).
Melt butter in a small pan until bubbling, stir in dried mint and Aleppo pepper for 20 seconds, and swirl generously atop the soup.

description: An ancient fermented grain soup prepared from sun-dried dough of yogurt, tomatoes, red peppers, and herbs. Rich in umami, tangy, and deeply restorative during winter months.

ingredients.name: Powdered Turkish Tarhana
ingredients.substitute: Available at Middle Eastern grocers/Amazon; or blend 1/4 cup Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup semolina flour, 1 tbsp tomato paste, and 1/2 tsp dried mint reconstituted

ingredients.name: Turkish Sweet Pepper Paste (Tatlı Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: 1 tsp tomato paste mixed with a pinch of smoked paprika

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Dried spearmint

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Crushed red pepper flakes

ingredients.name: Turkish Feta (Beyaz Peynir) or Kaşar cubes for topping
ingredients.substitute: French sheep's milk feta or mild white cheddar cubes

steps.instruction: In a bowl, soak the dry tarhana powder in 1 cup of cold water or broth for 15 minutes, whisking occasionally until fully softened and dissolved into a slurry.
Melt butter in a soup pot over medium heat. Add grated garlic, tomato paste, and pepper paste; sauté until fragrant and darkened in color.
Pour the remaining 4 cups of broth into the pot and bring to a simmer.
Gradually whisk the dissolved tarhana slurry into the hot broth. Reduce heat to medium-low and whisk continuously as it thickens to prevent sticking to the bottom.
Stir in dried spearmint and Aleppo pepper. Simmer gently on low for 5 minutes until creamy and fragrant.
Ladle into warm bowls and top with small cubes of crumbled feta or grated cheese and crunchy croutons.

titleEn: Velvety Tomato Soup with Melted Kaşar
description: Rich, silky Turkish bistro-style tomato soup made with a golden roux, ripe summer tomatoes, a touch of milk, and finished with a molten mound of aged kaşar cheese.

ingredients.name: Ripe Roma Tomatoes (grated or peeled & crushed)
ingredients.substitute: 1 can (28 oz) San Marzano whole peeled tomatoes, crushed

ingredients.name: Whole Milk
ingredients.substitute: Half-and-half or unsweetened oat milk

ingredients.name: Turkish Fresh Kaşar Cheese (Taze Kaşar)
ingredients.substitute: Low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella mixed with mild provolone or young Gouda

steps.instruction: In a pot, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in all-purpose flour and cook for 2 minutes until blond and nutty smelling.
Stir in tomato paste and cook with the roux for 1 minute until fragrant.
Gradually whisk in the crushed tomatoes and warm broth in a slow stream to prevent lumps from forming.
Add sugar, salt, and freshly cracked black pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then turn down heat and simmer partially covered until slightly thickened.
Blend with an immersion blender until velvety smooth. Slowly stir in warm whole milk and simmer for an additional 2 minutes without boiling.
Ladle into warm bowls and immediately crown each serving with a generous handful of freshly shredded kaşar cheese so it melts into stringy richness.

description: The ultimate Turkish restorative soup: tender shredded poached chicken thighs and toasted vermicelli noodles in a golden, lemon-scented broth infused with parsley and garlic.

ingredients.name: Bone-In Skinless Chicken Thighs or Breasts
Turkish Vermicelli Noodles (Tel Şehriye)
ingredients.substitute: Mexican fideo cut pasta or broken angel hair pasta nests

ingredients.name: Homemade Chicken Poaching Broth
ingredients.substitute: Store-bought low-sodium chicken stock

ingredients.name: Turkish Sweet Pepper Paste (Tatlı Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: 1 tsp tomato paste mixed with a pinch of paprika

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Dried spearmint

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Crushed red pepper flakes

steps.instruction: Place chicken thighs in a pot with 7 cups water, 1 peeled onion, and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, skim foam, then simmer on low until cooked through and fork tender.
Remove chicken to a plate to cool slightly. Strain the poaching stock through a sieve to yield 6 cups of clear chicken broth. Shred chicken meat into bite-sized shreds, discarding bones.
In your soup pot, melt butter over medium heat. Add tomato paste and pepper paste, sautéing for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour the strained hot chicken broth into the pot and bring to a lively simmer.
Add the tel şehriye (vermicelli) and shredded chicken. Cook on medium-low until the pasta is tender and cooked through.
Stir in fresh lemon juice, dried mint, Aleppo pepper, and finely chopped parsley. Turn off heat, let rest 3 minutes, and serve hot.

titleEn: Fiery Gaziantep Lamb Neck & Garlic Rice Soup
description: Gaziantep's legendary UNESCO-recognized dawn soup: ultra-tender slow-braised lamb neck, short-grain rice, abundant minced garlic, and rendered tallow ignited with fiery red pepper over blazing flames.

ingredients.name: Bone-in Lamb Neck or Lamb Shank
ingredients.substitute: Bone-in beef shank with marrow or lamb stew meat with bones

ingredients.name: Lamb Fat or Clarified Butter (Ghee)
ingredients.substitute: Ghee, duck fat, or beef tallow

ingredients.name: Short-Grain Baldo Rice (Pre-cooked tender)
ingredients.substitute: Cooked Calrose rice or Arborio rice

ingredients.name: Turkish Hot Pepper Paste (Acı Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: 1.5 tbsp tomato paste mixed with 1/2 tsp cayenne and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (İpek Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Sweet paprika mixed with 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper flakes

steps.instruction: Place lamb neck pieces in a large stockpot or pressure cooker with 7 cups water and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, skim impurities, and simmer gently until meat falls completely off the bone (2 hours on stovetop, or 45 mins in an Instant Pot).
Remove meat, discard bones, and shred meat into fine succulent strands. Strain and reserve the gelatin-rich lamb broth.
In individual copper or shallow steel soup pans (or a heavy saucepan), smear the bottom with 1 tablespoon of ghee/lamb fat.
Layer a generous portion of cooked rice, shredded lamb meat, crushed garlic paste, hot pepper paste, and Aleppo pepper flakes directly over the fat.
Place the pan over high flame and sizzle until the fat crackles and spices release their deep aroma, about 1 minute.
Pour boiling lamb broth directly over the sizzling meat and rice, letting it bubble furiously for 2 minutes. Remove from heat, squeeze lemon juice liberally, and serve smoking hot.

titleEn: Classic Tripe Soup with Garlic-Vinegar Liaison
description: The quintessential Istanbul night-owl cure: clean beef tripe slow-simmered to tender perfection, thickened with an egg-lemon terbiye, and spiked at the table with garlic vinegar and pepper butter.

ingredients.name: Cleaned Beef Tripe (İşkembe)
ingredients.substitute: Honeycomb or flat beef tripe (widely found in Hispanic and Asian supermarkets like H-Mart or 99 Ranch)

ingredients.name: Garlic (for soup stock and table sauce)
Red Wine Vinegar or White Grape Vinegar
Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Crushed red pepper flakes mixed with sweet paprika

steps.instruction: Thoroughly rinse tripe in cold water with vinegar. Place in a large pot with 8 cups water and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Bring to a boil, skim foam, cover and simmer until tripe is completely tender (about 90 minutes on stove, or 40 minutes in a pressure cooker).
Drain and cut the tender tripe into small bite-sized cubes (approx 1/2 inch). Strain the cooking broth and measure out 6 cups back into the clean pot.
Return cubed tripe to the simmering broth over medium-low heat.
Whisk the terbiye in a bowl: combine egg yolks, flour, milk or yogurt, and lemon juice until velvety smooth. Slowly ladle 2 cups of hot broth into the mixture while whisking constantly to temper.
Slowly pour the tempered liaison into the pot while stirring continuously. Simmer gently for 8 minutes until thickened; season with salt.

Prepare table garnishes: mix remaining crushed garlic with vinegar in a small bowl; melt butter with Aleppo pepper in a small skillet. Serve soup hot, inviting diners to spoon garlic-vinegar and chili butter to taste.

titleEn: Ottoman Wedding Lamb Soup with Lemon-Egg Liaison
description: Historically served at grand Ottoman wedding feasts, this rich soup showcases tender shredded lamb simmered in aromatic broth, thickened with flour, egg yolk, and lemon, and drizzled with scarlet paprika butter.

ingredients.name: Bone-in Lamb Shoulder or Lamb Neck
ingredients.substitute: Bone-in beef chuck roast or lamb shank

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Crushed red pepper flakes

steps.instruction: Place lamb pieces, carrot, and onion in a large pot with 7 cups water. Bring to a boil, skim scum thoroughly, cover and simmer over low heat until lamb is extraordinarily tender.
Remove lamb and vegetables. Finely shred the meat by hand, discarding fat and bones. Strain and measure 5 cups of the rich lamb broth.
In a clean soup pot, melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 2 minutes without browning to create a blond roux.
Gradually whisk the strained warm lamb broth into the roux until smooth and lump-free. Add the shredded lamb meat and bring to a gentle simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk egg yolks and lemon juice together. Temper with a ladle of hot soup, then stir back into the pot over low heat. Simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling; season with salt.
In a small pan, melt remaining 1 tablespoon butter with sweet paprika and Aleppo pepper until sizzling. Swirl over bowls and serve with fresh bread.

description: A magnificent feast dish of Gaziantep crafted during Eid: tiny hand-rolled rice-and-beef dumplings, stewed chickpeas, and shredded meat immersed in a rich, warm strained yogurt broth scented with dried mint.

ingredients.name: White Rice Flour
ingredients.substitute: Finely ground white rice (ground in a coffee/spice grinder)

ingredients.name: Cooked Chickpeas
ingredients.substitute: 1 can (15 oz) canned chickpeas, rinsed and drained

ingredients.name: Cubed Stewing Beef or Lamb (boiled tender)
Turkish Strained Yogurt (Süzme Yoğurt)
ingredients.substitute: Whole-milk Greek yogurt (e.g., Fage Total 5%)

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Dried spearmint

steps.instruction: In a food processor, blend ground beef, rice flour, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper into a smooth paste. Roll between oiled palms into chickpea-sized micro-meatballs (yuvalama köfte).
Place the tiny meatballs in a steamer basket over boiling water and steam for 10 minutes until set, or parboil briefly in water; drain and set aside.
In a soup pot, combine 4 cups beef/lamb broth, cooked chickpeas, and tender stewed meat chunks. Bring to a low simmer.
In a bowl, whisk Greek yogurt, egg, cornstarch, and 1/2 cup cold water. Gradually ladle hot broth into the yogurt to temper it thoroughly.

Pour the tempered yogurt into the simmering pot in a slow stream, stirring continuously in one direction over low heat until the soup reaches a bare simmer. Add the steamed micro-meatballs and cook gently for 5 minutes.
Turn off heat and season with salt. Melt butter in a skillet, sizzle dried mint for 20 seconds, and pour the fragrant green butter over the soup.

titleEn: Ancient Silk Road Green Lentil & Noodle Soup
description: Dating back to the Seljuk Turk era and Divanu Lugat'it-Turk, this hearty heritage soup combines green lentils, chickpeas, and handmade noodles in a tangy yogurt base, topped with caramelized onion and mint.

ingredients.name: Green or Brown Lentils (Yeşil Mercimek)
ingredients.substitute: French green Puy lentils or brown lentils

ingredients.name: Cooked Chickpeas
ingredients.substitute: Canned chickpeas, rinsed

ingredients.name: Turkish Egg Noodles (Erişte)
ingredients.substitute: Short German egg noodles, spätzle, or cut egg fettuccine

ingredients.name: Turkish Strained Yogurt (Süzme Yoğurt)
ingredients.substitute: Whole-milk Greek yogurt

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Dried spearmint

steps.instruction: In a pot, bring lentils and 6 cups water to a boil. Simmer over medium-low heat until lentils are tender but still retain their shape.
Add cooked chickpeas and erişte (egg noodles) to the pot. Simmer until the noodles are al dente.
Whisk yogurt, egg yolk, and flour in a bowl. Temper the mixture by slowly whisking in 2 ladles of hot broth from the pot.
Slowly pour the tempered yogurt mixture into the soup, stirring continuously in one direction until it gently simmers. Cook on low for 3 minutes, then remove from heat and season with salt.
In a skillet, melt butter and cook finely diced onions until golden brown and sweet.
Add dried spearmint and Aleppo pepper to the caramelized onions, sizzling for 30 seconds. Ladle soup into bowls and garnish with spoonfuls of the minty onion butter.

titleEn: Antakya Spiced Cumin & Coriander Red Lentil Soup
description: From the culinary crossroads of Hatay (Antakya), Mahluta features tender red lentils, cracked coriander, and a signature whole cumin-seed butter topping accompanied by caramelized onions.

ingredients.name: Turkish Sweet Pepper Paste (Tatlı Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: 1 tbsp tomato paste with 1/2 tsp smoked paprika

steps.instruction: Dice one onion and mince garlic. Heat olive oil in a soup pot over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant and softened.
Stir in pepper paste and ground coriander, cooking for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add washed red lentils and broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover and simmer until lentils completely disintegrate.
Whisk vigorously or lightly pulse with an immersion blender to achieve a rustic, semi-smooth textured puree. Season with salt and lemon juice.
Thinly slice the second onion into half-moons. In a skillet, melt butter over medium heat and fry the onions until dark golden and caramelized.
Add whole cumin seeds to the hot caramelized onion butter; let them crackle and toast for 45 seconds until intensely aromatic. Ladle soup into bowls and crown with the cumin-onion butter.

titleEn: Hearty Lamb Broth Soup with Garlic & Aleppo Pepper
description: An iconic Turkish powerhouse soup celebrated for its restorative properties: collagen-dense lamb shank and knuckle broth with tender shredded meat, finished with garlic-lemon liaison and spiced butter.

ingredients.name: Bone-in Lamb Shanks or Lamb Trotters/Neck
ingredients.substitute: Veal osso buco or beef shank marrow bones with meat

ingredients.name: Red Wine Vinegar
ingredients.substitute: Apple cider vinegar or grape vinegar

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Crushed red pepper flakes mixed with sweet paprika

steps.instruction: Place bone-in lamb pieces into a heavy pot with 8 cups water and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, skim foam, cover and simmer over low heat until meat is meltingly tender and marrow is rendered (90 minutes, or 45 mins in Instant Pot).
Transfer meat to a cutting board, shred into small morsels, and discard bones. Strain the rich broth through a fine-mesh sieve.
Return 6 cups of broth and the shredded meat to a clean pot and bring to a simmer.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, egg yolk, lemon juice, and 4 cloves of minced garlic. Slowly temper with two ladles of warm lamb broth while whisking.
Pour the tempered liaison into the pot, stirring constantly. Simmer gently on low for 5 minutes until glossy and slightly body-thickened; season with salt.
Make the table sauce: mix remaining 4 cloves minced garlic into vinegar. In a small pan, sizzle butter with Aleppo pepper for 30 seconds. Serve soup blazing hot with garlic-vinegar and chili butter.

titleEn: Village Green Lentil & Homemade Egg Noodle Soup
description: An authentic rustic Anatolian village soup combining earthy green lentils, toasted egg noodles, and sweet onions simmered in tomato-pepper broth and seasoned with fragrant dried mint.

ingredients.name: Green Lentils (Yeşil Mercimek)
ingredients.substitute: Brown lentils or French green lentils

ingredients.name: Turkish Egg Noodles (Erişte)
ingredients.substitute: Short cut egg noodles, spätzle, or broken fettuccine

ingredients.name: Turkish Sweet Pepper Paste (Tatlı Biber Salçası)
ingredients.substitute: 1 tbsp tomato paste mixed with 1/2 tsp smoked paprika

ingredients.name: Turkish Dried Spearmint (Kuru Nane)
ingredients.substitute: Dried spearmint

ingredients.name: Aleppo Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber)
ingredients.substitute: Red pepper flakes

steps.instruction: Rinse green lentils and place in a pot with 4 cups of water. Parboil for 10 minutes over medium heat; drain off dark cooking water to keep the final soup broth vibrant and clean.
In a large soup pot, heat olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat. Sauté finely diced onion until soft and golden.
Add tomato paste and pepper paste; sauté with onions for 2 minutes to cook out raw taste.
Pour in 6 cups broth and add the parboiled green lentils. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered until lentils are nearly tender.
Add the erişte (egg noodles) to the pot. Cook until noodles are tender, about 8-10 minutes.
In a small skillet, sizzle remaining butter with dried mint and Aleppo pepper for 30 seconds; swirl into the finished soup, adjust salt, and serve.

titleEn: Bosphorus Sea Bass Chowder with Lemon-Egg Liaison
description: Served along the shores of Istanbul's Bosphorus strait: fresh sea bass fillet and garden vegetables simmered in aromatic fish stock, enriched with a velvety lemon-egg terbiye and fresh dill.

ingredients.name: Fresh Sea Bass Fillets (Levrek) or Cod
ingredients.substitute: Black sea bass, striped bass, cod, or halibut

ingredients.name: Fish Broth or Light Vegetable Broth
ingredients.substitute: Good quality store-bought seafood stock or vegetable stock

steps.instruction: In a soup pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté finely diced onion, carrot, and celery until fragrant and softening.
Add diced potato, bay leaf, and fish stock. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer covered until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Cut sea bass fillets into 1-inch pieces. Gently slide fish into the simmering broth and poach softly until opaque and flakey.
In a bowl, whisk together egg yolk, flour, and lemon juice until smooth. Slowly ladle 1 cup of hot soup broth into the bowl while whisking briskly to temper.
Reduce pot heat to low. Gently pour tempered liaison into soup, stirring carefully so as not to break up delicate fish pieces. Simmer for 3 minutes until silkily thickened.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in fresh dill and season with salt and white pepper. Serve immediately with extra lemon wedges.
